items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: there was another band booked in there, Sammy Stewart's orchestra... So both bands met at the Plaza Hotel there... I remember that band, there was a young fella named Chu Berry, played tenor saxophone, playing with Sammy Stewart

ctx.x: on the streetcar in front of my house. So this particular day I went down to go to work, and I walked in and there had been a fire. And I saw my beautiful saxophone all curled up where it was burned up. All the instruments were burned up. So that meant that Trent's band were locked in Cleveland, Ohio without instruments. So, we were exploited by two or three groups, they gave benefit dances for us, and we --when the dance was all over, when you checked to see how much money you had in the pot, you had none. So…

And we stayed in Cleveland that whole winter. Finally Alphonso Trent's father got together and took us out to the King Factory in Cleveland, Ohio, and they bought everybody an instrument. His father, his people put up the money and got everybody in the band an instrument. Now Spring of 1930. We started a tour and we booked into Columbus, Ohio, and we get to Columbus, Ohio and there was another band booked in there, Sammy Stewart's orchestra and that was Sammy Stewart's home, he was a Chicago band, and his band…

So both bands met at the Plaza Hotel there, which was a hotel out on Long Street in Columbus, Ohio. I remember that band, there was a young fella named Chu Berry, played tenor saxophone, playing with Sammy Stewart, and there was a guy named Big Sydney Catlett, drummer. Played drums. In our band, we had our original band, the dance we supposed to play very few people showed up, that meant that we were locked there, we were booked there in a pocket and we had to use some form of ingenuity in trying to get out.
